steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three commonly cited causes of World War I:

1. Militarism and the arms race  
   • In the decades before 1914, Europe’s great powers—especially Germany, Britain, France, and Russia—expanded their armies and navies and developed detailed war plans.  
   • This growth in military capability and the belief that force could achieve national goals made a large-scale conflict more likely once a crisis arose.

2. The system of entangling alliances  
   • Two main alliance blocs formed: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain).  
   • What might have remained a localized dispute after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand quickly escalated because each state felt compelled to support its allies.

3. Nationalism and the Balkan powder keg (including the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand)  
   • Nationalist aspirations among Slavic peoples in the Balkans threatened the stability of Austria-Hungary and increased tensions with Serbia and its patron, Russia.  
   • The assassination of the archduke in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914, carried out by a Bosnian Serb nationalist, provided the immediate spark, but it ignited a situation already primed for war by nationalism, militarism, and alliance commitments.
